items.prompt:
A flaw in reasoning is a:
A) fallacy
B) claim
C) title

Evidence that is overstated or twisted is:
A) exaggerated/distorted
B) relevant
C) sufficient

The art of persuasion is called:
A) rhetoric
B) grammar
C) spelling

'Crime rose, so clearly the new mayor destroyed our city.' This is a:
A) false-cause fallacy
B) sound argument
C) relevant statistic

A speaker claims '100% of people love this product.' This evidence is:
A) exaggerated/distorted
B) perfectly reliable
C) irrelevant to products

Beyond the claim, you should evaluate a speaker's:
A) point of view, reasoning, evidence, and rhetoric
B) height
C) clothing
items.answer: A) point of view, reasoning, evidence, and rhetoric

solution.answer: A) point of view, reasoning, evidence, and rhetoric

items.prompt:
A speaker argues for a policy by warning, 'If we don't act, our children will live in ruins!' with no evidence. This mainly relies on:
A) an emotional (fear) appeal rather than sound evidence
B) strong data
C) a valid study
items.answer: A) an emotional (fear) appeal rather than sound evidence

steps: Fear appeal, no evidence. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) an emotional (fear) appeal rather than sound evidence

items.prompt:
Which speaker is MOST credible on a health claim?
A) one citing a large peer-reviewed study, acknowledging limits
B) one claiming '100% cured, guaranteed'
C) one attacking critics personally
items.answer: A) one citing a large peer-reviewed study, acknowledging limits

steps: Sound evidence, honest. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) one citing a large peer-reviewed study, acknowledging limits
